title: Retain engineering definition
description: Preserve an explicitly supplied engineering definition accepted by the selected authoring profile so later sessions can retrieve its identity, type, and authored content. This behavior retains the supplied content; defining a revision to an existing entity belongs to the revision behavior.
inputs: The selected governed model and intended state.
The entity identity, type, authored definition, and explicit request to save it.
preconditions: The entity representation is supported and its identity is acceptable within the selected model.
The request has identified the definition and scope to retain.
outputs: The retained definition with its subject and resulting model state identifiable.
An explicit retention outcome describing success or the known failure or incomplete scope.
behavior: Retain the explicitly supplied identity, entity type, and authored content independently of private conversation or authoring-session state.
Report a successful save only when retention of the requested definition is confirmed.
Make the saved definition available to later sessions while it remains in the retained governed scope, subject to the current-reliance and retirement boundaries in IR-001 and SR-001.

failure_behavior.condition: The record is unsupported or its identity is missing or conflicts with a distinct entity.
failure_behavior.outcome: Identify the unsupported or invalid input rather than representing it as an accepted saved definition.

failure_behavior.condition: The save fails or retention cannot be fully confirmed.
failure_behavior.outcome: Report the known outcome and affected scope without claiming that the complete requested definition was saved.

sources.basis: SR-001 requires explicitly saved definitions to survive the originating session, within IR-001's retained-model boundaries.
Apply the user-selected clarity and naming rule to this existing asset; refine its name and explanation without changing its identity, capability scope, or typed relationships.

Propose MOD-001 as the single accountable architectural responsibility for the existing behavior. This allocation preserves the Function definition and does not establish implementation or completed interface/AR coverage outside the IR-001 pilot.
